structure.heading: Cohort Outcomes and Treatment Efficacy Under the 2024 Heart Failure Clinical Pathway (Riverbend University Hospital)
text_content: **Cohort Outcomes and Treatment Efficacy Under the 2024 Heart Failure Clinical Pathway (Riverbend University Hospital)**

The analysis cohort comprises 1,248 adult patients discharged between 2024-01-01 and 2024-12-31 under the Heart Failure Pathway at Riverbend University Hospital. Inclusion required pathway enrollment at admission and discharge documentation; transfers out were excluded. The dataset captures inpatient management, discharge medications, and 30-day outcomes as recorded in the hospital electronic health record. Patient-level variables were harmonized for temporal comparisons by quarter (Q1–Q4 2024). As a single-center, pathway-focused review, the findings reflect Riverbend’s implementation and local case-mix; external generalizability should be contextualized to similar academic medical centers. Data completeness exceeded 95% for primary discharge and outcome fields and core process measures consistently.

Thirty-day all-cause readmission decreased from 17.9% in Q1 2024 to 13.2% in Q4 2024, an absolute reduction of 4.7 percentage points and a relative decrease of approximately 26.3%. This downward trend is a primary indicator of improved short-term patient stability under the pathway and supports effectiveness of coordinated discharge planning, medication reconciliation, and scheduled post-discharge follow-up. While causality cannot be definitively assigned in this observational review, temporal alignment with intensified guideline-directed interventions suggests meaningful clinical benefit. Operationally, reduced readmissions decreased acute-care demand and supports pathway adoption as a driver of measurable treatment efficacy. Further multivariable modeling is recommended to confirm.

The median length of stay under the pathway decreased from 4.6 days in Q1 2024 to 4.1 days in Q4 2024, representing a median reduction of 0.5 days per patient. Applied across the cohort of 1,248 patients, this differential corresponds to approximately 624 hospital bed-days conserved during the year (1,248 × 0.5). Reduced median LOS improved inpatient throughput and expanded capacity for elective admissions at Riverbend University Hospital. From a quality and operations perspective, sustaining this improvement warrants targeted strategies such as early discharge planning, standardized titration protocols, and monitoring post-discharge outcomes to ensure efficiency gains do not compromise patient care.

Immediate implications include targeted renal monitoring at admission and during uptitration of diuretics or renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system agents, plus reinforcement of laboratory-triggered escalation pathways to mitigate progression.

Protocol compliance for the discharge bundle showed measurable improvement across 2024: compliance rose from 58% in Q1 2024 to 84% in Q4 2024. This trend followed implementation of standardized checklists, electronic health record prompts, and interdisciplinary discharge huddles initiated in March 2024. Audit data indicate most gains were in medication reconciliation and patient education components; gaps remain in scheduled post-discharge follow-up doc.ation. Sustaining the increase will require quarterly compliance dashboards, designated bundle champions on each ward, and integration of compliance metrics in departmental performance reviews.
